cards.front: Which cells secrete PTH, and what is the main signal that controls its release?
cards.back: The **chief cells** of the parathyroid glands. A fall in **ionized calcium** is sensed by the **calcium-sensing receptor (CaSR)**, and PTH release rises within minutes. High phosphate also stimulates release; **calcitriol** suppresses PTH gene expression.
cards.back_pt: As **células principais** das paratireoides. Uma queda do **cálcio ionizado** é detectada pelo **receptor sensível ao cálcio (CaSR)**, e a liberação de PTH aumenta em minutos. O fosfato alto também estimula a liberação; o **calcitriol** suprime a expressão do gene do PTH.

cards.front: Osteoclasts have no PTH receptors. How does PTH still increase bone resorption?
cards.back: PTH binds receptors on **osteoblasts**. Osteoblasts then express more **RANKL** and less **osteoprotegerin (OPG)**. RANKL binds **RANK** on osteoclast precursors, so more osteoclasts form and resorb bone, releasing calcium and phosphate.
cards.back_pt: O PTH se liga a receptores nos **osteoblastos**. Os osteoblastos passam a expressar mais **RANKL** e menos **osteoprotegerina (OPG)**. O RANKL se liga ao **RANK** dos precursores de osteoclastos, que se formam em maior número e reabsorvem osso, liberando cálcio e fosfato.

cards.front: What are the steps that turn vitamin D into its active form, and what does the active form do?
cards.back: Skin (UVB) or diet → **liver 25-hydroxylase** → 25-OH vitamin D (storage form, measured for deficiency) → **renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase** (stimulated by PTH and low phosphate) → **1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D**. It mainly increases **gut absorption** of calcium and phosphate.
cards.back_pt: Pele (UVB) ou dieta → **25-hidroxilase hepática** → 25-OH vitamina D (forma de reserva, dosada na deficiência) → **1-alfa-hidroxilase renal** (estimulada pelo PTH e pelo fosfato baixo) → **1,25-(OH)2 vitamina D**. Ela aumenta principalmente a **absorção intestinal** de cálcio e fosfato.

cards.front: What is the most common cause of primary hyperparathyroidism, and how does it usually come to attention?
cards.back: A single **parathyroid adenoma** (less often hyperplasia, as in **MEN1/MEN2A**; carcinoma is rare). Most patients are found on **routine labs** with no symptoms. When symptoms occur: kidney stones, bone pain, abdominal complaints (constipation, ulcers, pancreatitis) and mood or thinking changes.
cards.back_pt: Um **adenoma de paratireoide** único (menos vezes hiperplasia, como na **NEM1/NEM2A**; o carcinoma é raro). A maioria é descoberta em **exames de rotina**, sem sintomas. Quando há sintomas: cálculos renais, dor óssea, queixas abdominais (constipação, úlceras, pancreatite) e alterações de humor ou cognição.

cards.back: Bone disease of severe, long-standing **hyperparathyroidism**. Bone removed by heavy osteoclast activity is replaced by **fibrous tissue** and cysts; bleeding with giant cells and hemosiderin forms **brown tumors**. X-ray: **subperiosteal resorption** of the phalanges and a *salt-and-pepper* skull.
cards.back_pt: Doença óssea do **hiperparatireoidismo** grave e prolongado. O osso removido pela intensa atividade osteoclástica é substituído por **tecido fibroso** e cistos; hemorragia com células gigantes e hemossiderina forma os **tumores marrons**. Radiografia: **reabsorção subperiosteal** das falanges e crânio em *sal e pimenta* (*salt-and-pepper*).

cards.front: What is tertiary hyperparathyroidism, and how do its labs differ from secondary hyperparathyroidism?
cards.back: After years of **secondary hyperparathyroidism** (usually CKD), the hyperplastic glands secrete PTH **autonomously**, no longer suppressed by calcium. Secondary: **low or normal calcium**. Tertiary: **high calcium** with very high PTH. Classic setting: persistent hypercalcemia after **kidney transplant**.
cards.back_pt: Após anos de **hiperparatireoidismo secundário** (geralmente DRC), as glândulas hiperplásicas secretam PTH de forma **autônoma**, sem supressão pelo cálcio. Secundário: **cálcio baixo ou normal**. Terciário: **cálcio alto** com PTH muito alto. Cenário clássico: hipercalcemia persistente após **transplante renal**.

cards.front: Why does DiGeorge syndrome cause neonatal hypocalcemia?
cards.back: A **22q11.2 deletion** disrupts development of the **3rd and 4th pharyngeal pouches**. The parathyroid glands (and thymus) are absent or underdeveloped, so PTH is low: **hypocalcemia** with high phosphate. Other features: T-cell deficiency, conotruncal heart defects, facial anomalies.
cards.back_pt: Uma **deleção 22q11.2** prejudica o desenvolvimento das **3ª e 4ª bolsas faríngeas**. As paratireoides (e o timo) estão ausentes ou hipoplásicas, então o PTH fica baixo: **hipocalcemia** com fosfato alto. Outros achados: deficiência de linfócitos T, defeitos cardíacos conotruncais, anomalias faciais.

cards.front: What are the three main mechanisms of hypercalcemia of malignancy?
cards.back: 1) **PTHrP** secretion (squamous cell carcinomas, renal and breast cancer). 2) **Osteolytic bone metastases** or myeloma (local bone destruction). 3) Tumor production of **1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D** (some **lymphomas**). In all three, PTH is **suppressed**.
cards.back_pt: 1) Secreção de **PTHrP** (carcinomas escamosos, câncer renal e de mama). 2) **Metástases ósseas osteolíticas** ou mieloma (destruição óssea local). 3) Produção tumoral de **1,25-(OH)2 vitamina D** (alguns **linfomas**). Nos três, o PTH está **suprimido**.

questions.stem: A 36-year-old man is found to have a high serum calcium on routine blood tests. He feels well and has no history of kidney stones or fractures. He takes no medications or supplements. His mother and his brother were also told they have mildly high calcium, and his brother's neck surgery did not correct it. Serum calcium is 10.9 mg/dL (normal 8.5-10.5), phosphate is 2.8 mg/dL (normal 2.5-4.5), and PTH is in the upper part of the normal range. Creatinine is normal. His 24-hour urinary calcium excretion is very low. Which mechanism best explains his findings?
choices: Autonomous PTH secretion by a single parathyroid adenoma
Loss-of-function mutation in the calcium-sensing receptor
Tumor secretion of PTH-related peptide
Increased renal calcium reabsorption caused by a thiazide diuretic
Excess 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D production by granulomas
questions.explanation: This is **familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia (FHH)**, an autosomal dominant **inactivating CaSR mutation**. The parathyroid glands and kidneys 'see' a normal calcium as low, so PTH stays normal or mildly high and the kidneys keep calcium (**very low urinary calcium**). A parathyroid adenoma is the most tempting answer, but it usually causes **high** urinary calcium, and in FHH parathyroid surgery does not cure the hypercalcemia, as in his brother.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **hipercalcemia hipocalciúrica familiar (HHF)**, uma **mutação inativadora do CaSR** de herança autossômica dominante. As paratireoides e os rins 'interpretam' um cálcio normal como baixo, então o PTH fica normal ou levemente alto e os rins retêm cálcio (**calciúria muito baixa**). O adenoma de paratireoide é a resposta mais tentadora, mas geralmente causa calciúria **alta**, e na HHF a cirurgia das paratireoides não corrige a hipercalcemia, como no irmão.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman had a total thyroidectomy with central neck lymph node dissection for papillary thyroid carcinoma. On the second day after surgery she reports tingling around her mouth and in her fingertips, and painful muscle cramps in her hands. Serum calcium is 6.9 mg/dL (normal 8.5-10.5) with normal albumin, phosphate is 5.6 mg/dL (normal 2.5-4.5), and magnesium is normal. Serum PTH is undetectable. Which mechanism best explains her low calcium?
choices: Release of stored calcitonin from the manipulated thyroid gland
Rapid calcium uptake by bone after removal of excess thyroid hormone
Removal of, or loss of blood supply to, the parathyroid glands
End-organ resistance to parathyroid hormone
Reduced intake of vitamin D during the first days after surgery
questions.explanation: Low calcium, **high phosphate** and an **undetectable PTH** after neck surgery point to **surgical hypoparathyroidism**: the glands were removed or lost their blood supply during the operation. **Hungry bone syndrome** is the most tempting alternative, but it typically follows surgery for long-standing hyperparathyroidism (and, less often, thyroidectomy for severe hyperthyroidism), and it causes **low** phosphate as bone takes up both minerals; this patient had cancer, not hyperthyroidism. PTH resistance would give a high PTH, and calcitonin has only a minor effect on calcium in humans.
questions.explanation_pt: Cálcio baixo, **fosfato alto** e **PTH indetectável** após cirurgia cervical indicam **hipoparatireoidismo cirúrgico**: as glândulas foram retiradas ou perderam a irrigação durante a operação. A **síndrome da fome óssea** (*hungry bone*) é a alternativa mais tentadora, mas costuma ocorrer após cirurgia de hiperparatireoidismo prolongado (e, menos vezes, tireoidectomia por hipertireoidismo grave), e causa fosfato **baixo**, pois o osso capta os dois minerais; esta paciente tinha câncer, não hipertireoidismo. A resistência ao PTH daria PTH alto, e a calcitonina tem efeito apenas pequeno sobre o cálcio em humanos.

questions.stem: A 10-year-old girl is evaluated for short stature and episodes of muscle cramps. She has a round face, a short neck, obesity, and mild learning difficulties. When she makes a fist, the knuckles of her fourth and fifth fingers are missing because those metacarpals are short. Serum calcium is 7.2 mg/dL (normal 8.5-10.5), phosphate is 6.4 mg/dL (normal for age 3.7-5.6), magnesium is normal, and PTH is markedly elevated. Renal function is normal. What is the most likely underlying defect?
choices: Deletion of chromosome 22q11.2
Autoimmune destruction of the parathyroid glands
Inactivating mutation of the calcium-sensing receptor
Mutation in PHEX causing excess FGF23
Mutation in GNAS that impairs Gs-alpha signaling
questions.explanation: Low calcium and high phosphate despite a **high PTH** mean the tissues do not respond to PTH: **pseudohypoparathyroidism type 1A**. A **GNAS** mutation (inherited from the **mother**) impairs the **Gs-alpha** protein that links the PTH receptor to cAMP. The body features are **Albright hereditary osteodystrophy**: short stature, round face, obesity and **short 4th/5th metacarpals**. DiGeorge syndrome and autoimmune destruction also cause low calcium and high phosphate, but with a **low** PTH.
questions.explanation_pt: Cálcio baixo e fosfato alto apesar de **PTH alto** indicam que os tecidos não respondem ao PTH: **pseudo-hipoparatireoidismo tipo 1A**. Uma mutação em **GNAS** (herdada da **mãe**) prejudica a proteína **Gs-alfa**, que liga o receptor do PTH ao AMPc. Os achados corporais são da **osteodistrofia hereditária de Albright**: baixa estatura, face arredondada, obesidade e **4º e 5º metacarpos curtos**. A síndrome de DiGeorge e a destruição autoimune também causam cálcio baixo e fosfato alto, mas com PTH **baixo**.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has 8 months of diffuse bone aches and difficulty climbing stairs. She had a Roux-en-Y gastric bypass 7 years ago and stopped taking her vitamin supplements soon after. She walks with a waddling gait, and pressing on her tibias is painful. Serum calcium is 8.4 mg/dL (normal 8.5-10.5) and alkaline phosphatase is elevated. A pelvic x-ray shows narrow lucent lines perpendicular to the cortex of both pubic rami. Which additional set of laboratory findings is most likely?
choices: Low 25-hydroxyvitamin D, high PTH, low phosphate
Low 25-hydroxyvitamin D, low PTH, high phosphate
Normal 25-hydroxyvitamin D, high PTH, high phosphate
High 25-hydroxyvitamin D, low PTH, high phosphate
Normal 25-hydroxyvitamin D, normal PTH, low phosphate
questions.explanation: Bone pain, proximal weakness, high alkaline phosphatase and **pseudofractures** (*Looser zones*) after gastric bypass point to **osteomalacia** from **vitamin D deficiency**. Low calcium absorption triggers **secondary hyperparathyroidism**; PTH keeps calcium near normal but makes the kidney waste phosphate, so phosphate is **low**. The tempting choice with high PTH and **high** phosphate fits CKD, not vitamin D deficiency. Serum 1,25-(OH)2 vitamin D can be normal here because PTH stimulates 1-alpha-hydroxylase, so **25-OH vitamin D** is the test for deficiency.
questions.explanation_pt: Dor óssea, fraqueza proximal, fosfatase alcalina alta e **pseudofraturas** (*zonas de Looser*) após bypass gástrico indicam **osteomalácia** por **deficiência de vitamina D**. A baixa absorção de cálcio desencadeia **hiperparatireoidismo secundário**; o PTH mantém o cálcio perto do normal, mas faz o rim perder fosfato, então o fosfato fica **baixo**. A alternativa tentadora com PTH alto e fosfato **alto** corresponde à DRC, não à deficiência de vitamina D. A 1,25-(OH)2 vitamina D sérica pode estar normal aqui, pois o PTH estimula a 1-alfa-hidroxilase; por isso a **25-OH vitamina D** é o exame para a deficiência.

notes.title: Parathyroid and calcium: hormones and disorders
notes.body_md:
## Hormones

- **PTH** (chief cells): released when **ionized calcium** falls (sensed by the **CaSR**). It increases bone resorption (via osteoblast **RANKL**), calcium reabsorption in the distal tubule, **phosphate wasting** in the proximal tubule, and renal **1-alpha-hydroxylase**.
- **Vitamin D**: skin or diet → 25-OH in the **liver** → **1,25-(OH)2** in the **kidney**. It raises gut absorption of calcium and phosphate. Measure **25-OH vitamin D** to find deficiency.
- **Calcitonin** (thyroid parafollicular C cells): inhibits osteoclasts; only a minor role in normal calcium control.

## Too much PTH

- **Primary**: usually a single **adenoma**. High calcium, **low phosphate**, high PTH. Often found on routine labs. Symptomatic cases: kidney stones, bone pain, abdominal complaints, mood changes, and **osteitis fibrosa cystica** (brown tumors, subperiosteal resorption).
- **Secondary**: a normal response to low calcium, as in **CKD** (high phosphate, low calcitriol; bone disease is **renal osteodystrophy**) or vitamin D deficiency (low phosphate).
- **Tertiary**: glands become **autonomous** after long secondary disease; calcium becomes **high**.

## Too little PTH effect

- **Hypoparathyroidism**: low calcium, high phosphate, **low PTH**. Causes: neck surgery, autoimmune disease, **DiGeorge** (3rd/4th pouches).
- **Pseudohypoparathyroidism 1A**: same calcium and phosphate, but **high PTH** (resistance). **GNAS** mutation; **Albright hereditary osteodystrophy** with short 4th/5th metacarpals.

## Other hypercalcemia

- **Malignancy**: PTHrP, osteolytic metastases, or calcitriol from lymphoma. PTH is suppressed.
- **FHH**: inactivating **CaSR** mutation; mild high calcium, normal or slightly high PTH, **very low urinary calcium**. Parathyroidectomy does not help.

## Soft bones

- **Rickets** (children, open growth plates) and **osteomalacia** (adults): poor mineralization of new bone matrix, usually from **vitamin D deficiency**.
- **X-linked hypophosphatemic rickets**: **PHEX** mutation raises **FGF23**, so the kidney wastes phosphate and makes less calcitriol. Calcium is normal; vitamin D supplements alone do not correct it.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Hormônios

- **PTH** (células principais): liberado quando o **cálcio ionizado** cai (detectado pelo **CaSR**). Aumenta a reabsorção óssea (via **RANKL** dos osteoblastos), a reabsorção de cálcio no túbulo distal, a **perda renal de fosfato** no túbulo proximal e a **1-alfa-hidroxilase** renal.
- **Vitamina D**: pele ou dieta → 25-OH no **fígado** → **1,25-(OH)2** no **rim**. Aumenta a absorção intestinal de cálcio e fosfato. Dosar a **25-OH vitamina D** para diagnosticar deficiência.
- **Calcitonina** (células C parafoliculares da tireoide): inibe os osteoclastos; papel apenas pequeno no controle normal do cálcio.

## Excesso de PTH

- **Primário**: geralmente um **adenoma** único. Cálcio alto, **fosfato baixo**, PTH alto. Muitas vezes descoberto em exames de rotina. Casos sintomáticos: cálculos renais, dor óssea, queixas abdominais, alterações de humor e **osteíte fibrosa cística** (tumores marrons, reabsorção subperiosteal).
- **Secundário**: resposta normal ao cálcio baixo, como na **DRC** (fosfato alto, calcitriol baixo; a doença óssea é a **osteodistrofia renal**) ou na deficiência de vitamina D (fosfato baixo).
- **Terciário**: as glândulas tornam-se **autônomas** após doença secundária prolongada; o cálcio fica **alto**.

## Pouco efeito do PTH

- **Hipoparatireoidismo**: cálcio baixo, fosfato alto, **PTH baixo**. Causas: cirurgia cervical, doença autoimune, **DiGeorge** (3ª e 4ª bolsas).
- **Pseudo-hipoparatireoidismo 1A**: mesmo cálcio e fosfato, mas **PTH alto** (resistência). Mutação em **GNAS**; **osteodistrofia hereditária de Albright** com 4º e 5º metacarpos curtos.

## Outras hipercalcemias

- **Neoplasias**: PTHrP, metástases osteolíticas ou calcitriol produzido por linfoma. O PTH está suprimido.
- **HHF**: mutação inativadora do **CaSR**; cálcio levemente alto, PTH normal ou pouco elevado, **calciúria muito baixa**. A paratireoidectomia não ajuda.

## Ossos moles

- **Raquitismo** (crianças, placas de crescimento abertas) e **osteomalácia** (adultos): mineralização deficiente da nova matriz óssea, geralmente por **deficiência de vitamina D**.
- **Raquitismo hipofosfatêmico ligado ao X**: mutação em **PHEX** eleva o **FGF23**, então o rim perde fosfato e produz menos calcitriol. O cálcio é normal; suplementos de vitamina D sozinhos não corrigem o quadro.
